title: Changing only the case or punctuation of a part's own number saves
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • Active part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-OWNNUM-01), with the description {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL Own Number), is stocked at {Location-A} and at no other location.
  • No other part at {Location-A} has a number that matches {Part-A} once upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored.
  • {Number-A} (for example zzautotest-pl-ownnum-01) is {Part-A} in lower case, and {Number-B} (for example ZZAUTOTESTPLOWNNUM01) is {Part-A} without its hyphens.
  • No Part Library entry has exactly the number {Number-A} or {Number-B}.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Parts → Inventory and type {Part-A} in the search.
  2. Click the {Part-A} row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with {Number-A}.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Type {Number-A} in the search.
  6. Click the {Number-A} row.
  7. Replace the Part Number with {Number-B}.
  8. Click Save.
  9. Type {Number-B} in the search.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the save goes through: no "{Part-A} already exists at this location." message appears, and the window closes.
  • Step 5: one row shows Part Number {Number-A} with Description {Description-A}: the same part, renamed.
  • Step 8: the save goes through: no "already exists at this location" message appears, and the window closes.
  • Step 9: one row shows Part Number {Number-B} with Description {Description-A}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S7-N5c, S7-N5b, S7-N3, §4 Key Decisions, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.2 (Both fields edited), 13 Oct copy. Product's 9 Oct answer (Chris Ward, question 11). Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S7-N5c: “The check never counts the part being saved. Changing a part's number only in upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods or spaces, for example FF-5507 to FF5507, saves when no other part at the location matches it.”
  • S7-N5b: “S7-N3 and S7-N4 apply when a part is created and when its part number is changed. Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused by them, even when the location already holds a part whose number matches it.”
  • S7-N3: “If a part with the same number is already stocked at this location and is active, the save is refused with "{part number} already exists at this location."”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions (duplicate at the location): “A new part number already stocked at the location is refused, ignoring case and punctuation. This check stops a second copy of a part at one location. It runs when a part is created or its number is changed, never when a part is saved with its number unchanged.”
